source_authority.document: Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science
loci: Chapter 3 Theorem 1.1 states that the unit group L_F2(1,2)^x is not sofic; it does not state that a finitely presented nonsofic group exists.
The introduction states that the proof constructs a finitely generated nonsofic subgroup G of the unit group.

For the specific complete nine-word code D, the source defines G = EL_D(R) = Theta_D(EL_9(R)) <= R^x and records G isomorphic to EL_9(R); the proof later concludes this G, and hence R^x, is not sofic.

The source defines normalized Hamming distance on a nonempty finite set and a countable-group sofic approximation by maps p_n with p_n(1)=1, multiplicative error tending to zero, and nonidentity separation tending to one.

definition_concordance.sofic_convention: Lean normalizedHamming is Hamming disagreement count divided by the finite model size. GoodOn requires epsilon-multiplicativity on a finite test set and moves every tested nonidentity element on more than 1-epsilon of points. Sofic quantifies over every finite F and every 0<epsilon<1. This is the local finite-piece form of the source convention. For countable groups, nonempty_soficApproximation_of_sofic explicitly converts the Lean property to the source-style sequence by a finite exhaustion and epsilon_n=1/(n+2).
definition_concordance.source_nonsofic_carrier: The source obstruction group is G = EL_D(R), isomorphic to EL_9(R). Lean binaryLeavittElementaryGroup 9 is elementaryGroup (Fin 9) BinaryLeavitt, and ninePrefixElementaryGroupEquiv supplies the corresponding nine-prefix group equivalence. binaryLeavittElementaryGroup_not_sofic transports the formal source obstruction through this carrier equivalence rather than identifying R^x definitionally with EL_9(R).
definition_concordance.finite_obstruction: exists_finite_obstruction negates the Lean Sofic approximation quantifiers to obtain a finite F containing 1 and an epsilon with 0<epsilon<1 for which no PermutationModel is GoodOn. This is an internal compact finite failure certificate; it is not a claim printed in Chapter 3.
definition_concordance.table_group: From finite F, multiplicationTable F is finite and tableRelators F h1 is a finite set of free-group relations encoding the identity and the multiplication table on F. tableGroup F h1 is PresentedGroup of those relators. tableGroup_not_sofic_of_obstruction proves that a sofic approximation of this table group would pull back to a forbidden GoodOn model for F.
definition_concordance.finite_presentation: At the pinned Mathlib commit, Group.IsFinitelyPresented G means that for some finite n there is a surjective homomorphism FreeGroup (Fin n) -> G whose kernel is the normal closure of finitely many relations. tableGroup_finitelyPresented is obtained by the standard PresentedGroup finite-generator/finite-relator instance, so the target uses the ordinary group-theoretic meaning of finitely presented.
definition_concordance.universe_and_existence: The general theorem exists_finitelyPresented_not_sofic_of_not_sofic preserves the source group's universe. The instantiated binaryLeavittElementaryGroup 9 lives in Type, so its table-group witness satisfies the Comparator's existential G : Type with an actual Group instance; no universe lift or empty existential carrier is hidden.

target_audits.source_relation: Chapter 3 proves the unit group nonsofic and explicitly constructs a finitely generated nonsofic subgroup G isomorphic to EL_9(R). It does not state the existence of a finitely presented nonsofic group as Theorem 1.1 or as the displayed source conclusion audited here.
target_audits.formal_relation: The target is exactly discharged by exists_finitelyPresented_not_sofic_of_not_sofic binaryLeavittElementaryGroup_not_sofic. The first theorem constructs a new finitely presented nonsofic PresentedGroup from a finite failed sofic test; the second is the formal source obstruction on the EL_9(R) carrier. The resulting existential is therefore a justified formal consequence of the source nonsofic construction, not a verbatim projection of Theorem 1.1.

evidence: binaryLeavittElementaryGroup 9 is a concrete countable group carrier corresponding to the source EL_9(R) obstruction group.

binaryLeavittElementaryGroup_not_sofic proves an actual negation of the Lean Sofic property for that carrier; the antecedent supplied to the finite-obstruction theorem is therefore inhabited evidence, not an impossible hypothesis.
exists_finite_obstruction returns a finite test set containing 1 and a strict error parameter 0<epsilon<1.
tableRelators is a Finset and tableGroup is a concrete PresentedGroup with a Group instance; tableGroup_finitelyPresented supplies the standard finite-presentation property.
tableGroup_not_sofic_of_obstruction derives an actual contradiction from any putative Sofic instance by pulling its finite test model back to the original obstruction.
The final existential supplies both the concrete group structure and the conjunction Group.IsFinitelyPresented H and not Sofic H.

proof_path_evidence: binaryLeavittElementaryGroup_not_sofic is the exact source-side nonsofic input to the target.
exists_finite_obstruction extracts a single finite failed approximation test from not Sofic.
tableRelators constructs finitely many identity and multiplication-table relators on the finite multiplicationTable F generator type.
tableGroup_finitelyPresented is the pinned Mathlib PresentedGroup finite-presentation instance.
goodOn_pullbackTableModel shows that a GoodOn model of the table group induces a GoodOn model of the original finite obstruction.
tableGroup_not_sofic_of_obstruction uses that pullback to prove the table group nonsofic.
exists_nonsofic_finite_table packages finite presentation and nonsoficity, and exists_finitelyPresented_not_sofic_of_not_sofic preserves the universe while emitting the existential target witness.
The registered target is exactly `exact SoficGroups.exists_finitelyPresented_not_sofic_of_not_sofic binaryLeavittElementaryGroup_not_sofic`.

replay_and_axiom_audit.authority_limit: Replay establishes exact formal-carrier and kernel-acceptance evidence only; it does not independently certify proof correctness or source-semantic equivalence.

disposition.basis: The registered target is a valid derived consequence at the audited boundary. Chapter 3 supplies a concrete nonsofic obstruction group G isomorphic to EL_9(R); the formal carrier realizes that group and proves its nonsoficity under the aligned finite-permutation approximation convention. A separate formal finite-obstruction/table-presentation argument then converts any nonsofic group into a finitely presented nonsofic PresentedGroup using the pinned standard Mathlib notion of finite presentation. The finite-presentation existential is therefore admitted only as a formal consequence, not as source Theorem 1.1 text.

claim_boundary: This candidate is limited to current-root semantic/nonvacuity classification of the single registered OTP-D-NON-SOFIC target. It binds Lean's local finite-set/epsilon permutation approximation property to the source sofic convention and records the explicit countable-group conversion to source-style approximation sequences. It identifies the source obstruction group only up to the proved EL_D(R) / EL_9(R) carrier equivalence and does not definitionally identify the full Leavitt unit group with EL_9(R). Most importantly, it does not attribute finite presentation to Chapter 3 Theorem 1.1: the target's finitely presented witness is created by the separate formal finite-obstruction and finite multiplication-table PresentedGroup construction after source-root nonsoficity has been established. The pinned Mathlib Group.IsFinitelyPresented definition is the standard finite-generators/finitely-many-normal-relations notion. This candidate creates no MATHSOLVE handoff, MATHCERT route or output, proof certification, mathematical-proof promotion, whole-chapter equivalence, or aggregate OpenAI Ten Proofs authority.
